Definition: from a derivative of G136 (in its primary sense); an obscure saying ("enigma"), i.e. (abstractly) obscureness:--X darkly.
BiblicalUsage: Once, in the most quoted verse about love's limits: For now we see through a glass, darkly. The word is enigma — a riddle, an obscure saying.
TheologicalSignificance: One riddle-word in one verse carries no doctrine of its own; its weight is Paul's promise that the dim glass gives way to seeing face to face.
